objective: Produce a technical decision document that captures system design direction, architectural constraints, and engineering trade-offs for this topic — forming a complete, self-consistent technical decision document for this architecture direction.

role.instruction: You are acting as a technical decision maker. Frame all questions and analyses from the perspective of system design, architectural constraints, and engineering trade-offs. Use technical vocabulary (architecture, dependencies, interfaces, rollback) rather than product vocabulary.

domain.name: technical
domain.instruction: Frame all gate dialogue and decision-doc content from the perspective of system design and engineering trade-offs for this architecture topic, which may span multiple future features. Technical identifiers, architecture terms, and implementation references are appropriate in this domain.

acceptance_criteria.goal: Whether this architecture direction can support follow-on work can be determined objectively.
acceptance_criteria.question: What observable and verifiable technical signals would show that this architecture direction is sound enough to support follow-on work?
acceptance_criteria.completion: Complete when 3–6 direction-level criteria cover the intended architectural outcomes and critical constraints, each verifiable through observable system behavior or evidence—not subjective judgment, feature-level implementation details, individual test names, or assertions.

impact_surface.goal: All technical change surfaces required to realize and verify this architecture direction are made explicit.
impact_surface.question: Which responsibility surfaces and implementation-stack layers does this architecture decision affect, and how do they map to each other?
impact_surface.completion: Complete when all affected systems, interfaces, and external parties are identified and mapped at subsystem or architecture-domain level, spanning potential future features—not modules, files, or test cases.

external_dependencies.goal: Cross-cutting dependencies this direction commits to have explicit and verifiable commitments.
external_dependencies.question: Which cross-cutting capabilities or components does this direction rely on, who owns them, and what must each dependency provide, change, or preserve?
external_dependencies.completion: Complete when every genuine cross-cutting dependency specifies its owner, required behavior or state—including changes such as upgrades—contract, authoritative source, and confirmation mechanism; unresolved facts are recorded as Assumptions. Exclude feature-specific integration details.

implementation_sketch.goal: The architecture direction has a coherent shape, with its structural constraints and reversibility understood.
implementation_sketch.question: What key architectural changes realize this direction, how do they work together, what non-obvious constraints or complexity shape them, and how reversible is committing to it?
implementation_sketch.completion: Complete when the direction's shape, key structural interactions, critical constraints or complexity, and reversibility are explicit, and unresolved constraints are recorded as Assumptions; remain at direction-shape level—not a concrete implementation plan, files, tasks, or patches.

gap_check.goal: No mismatch between the proposed architecture direction and the acceptance criteria remains hidden.
gap_check.question: Does the proposed architecture direction satisfy every acceptance criterion, and where does it fall short?
gap_check.completion: Complete when all acceptance criteria have been checked against the proposed architecture direction and a one-line verdict records either full coverage or any shortfall—without a separate breakdown.
